Subject: Clarify where requests are processed + deletion timing

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. Before we move to procurement we'd like a short written summary covering: which geographic regions customer inference requests may be processed in (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private), a list of subprocessors involved in the inference path, and the deletion/retention guarantees for request data and any associated logs.

Two specific asks from our security/compliance team:
- Can you confirm if any part of a request from a US customer will be routed to EU/Asia for processing?
- We need an expected timeline for permanent deletion after a deletion request (and what is actually deleted vs. cached/transient).

I'm attaching a short checklist the team uses. Would you be able to return a single PDF or CSV that maps the processing hops and retention windows?

Thanks,
Alex Murray
Director, Security & Compliance
Skyline Health

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.example.com>

Hi Alex — great question, and happy to put this into a short mapping. High level summary up front, then I'll attach a CSV map and SOC2 excerpt in a follow-up message.

High level:
- Routing: For Redwood Hosted API customers we route requests to a region selected by customer preference or lowest-latency policy. For US customers that is typically us-west-2 (Oregon) or us-east-1 (N. Virginia) — we will not route inference execution to EU/APAC unless explicitly configured by the customer or region policy requires it.
- Dedicated: When you purchase Redwood Dedicated we deploy in your reserved region(s) only — no cross-region processing.
- Private: For Private/VPC deployments the control plane is customer-managed and inference runs entirely on-prem or in your cloud project; no Redwood-hosted subprocessors see inference payloads.

Typical subprocessors in Hosted mode (examples — full roster attached):
- Cloud compute & object storage: AWS (EC2, S3 in us-west-2/us-east-1), GCP (optional customer-configured zones)
- CDN / edge: Cloudflare (for static assets and SDK downloads)
- Monitoring & tracing: Datadog (metrics/traces), Sentry (optional error forwarding)
- Telemetry ingestion: Segment (aggregated usage telemetry — can be disabled)
- Secrets/KMS: AWS KMS or customer-managed Cloud HSM (for Private)

Data residency notes:
- Inference execution (model weights, activations, KV cache) runs on the GPU host in the selected region. We do not ship model activations across regions for standard requests.
- KV cache used for prefix caching is kept in-memory on the runtime host and is ephemeral; it is not written to object storage.
- Request logs (request metadata, timestamps, diagnostic traces) are retained for debugging and billing and by default stored encrypted in S3 for 30 days for Hosted customers; we can extend this or shorten it per contract.

Deletion SLA:
- Customer-initiated deletion (via API or Console) triggers:
  1) Immediate deletion from active query logs and customer-visible records (<24 hours).
  2) Background job that removes entries from S3 and indexes within 7–30 days depending on the storage tier and replication windows.
  3) Cryptographic destruction/retire keys on rotation cycle for backups (90 days) — we provide attestation of lifecycle events.

I'll attach a CSV that enumerates per-region subprocessors and an excerpt from our SOC 2 pack. If you want a stricter EU-only processing commitment we can provide a regional routing contract (common for large health customers).

Thanks — sending the attachments now.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Alex — quick follow-up with the evidence pack and tighter language per our internal review.

Summary changes (per Monica / Product Security):
- Segment/Telemetry: By default we collect anonymized usage telemetry; for customers in regulated sectors we disable Segment on account creation and offer an "opt-in" toggle. Confirm whether you'd like it disabled for Skyline.
- Deletion SLA (finalized):
  • Immediate: customer-visible records removed within 24 hours.
  • Storage removal: objects moved to standard S3 lifecycle are fully removed within 30 days maximum (most entries are purged within 7–14 days depending on replication).
  • Backups & replicas: final cryptographic destruction of key material and backup rotations occur within 90 days; we provide a compliance attestation on request.
- Cross-border: For a US Skyline tenant using Hosted API with default routing, execution does not leave US regions. If you require contractual EU-only or APAC-only execution we can enable region lock and provide an addendum.

Attachments included: region_subprocessors_20280320.csv (per-region breakdown), SOC2_summary_redwood.pdf (excerpt), and a short one-page mapping exported to the folder below.
